findings.question: Is there ANY path where the +15d conservative bound is insufficient? Is half-month END + 15 days the right arithmetic file by file?
findings.disagrees_with: A3 F3 frozen constant MIN_CONDITIONING_GUARD_DAYS=16 as a SUFFICIENT minimum; A3's 17d 'conservative' guard is currently advisory
findings.finding: The frozen bound posting_bound(file) = half_month_end + 15d is NOT uniformly watertight against the page's OWN cadence text (re-verified byte-exact from the pinned HTML). File-by-file arithmetic: (a) 'a' files, month M (settlements M/01..M/15 window; measured cnsfails202608a last settlement 8/14, nominal close 8/15): page promises 'available at the end of the month'. In 31-day months (7 of 12) the promise is M/31 but the frozen bound is M/15+15 = M/30 - the bound UNDERSTATES the page's own promise by 1 day. The packet's arithmetic is confirmed: real posting can be up to 17 days after the LAST settlement (8/31 minus 8/14 = 17d). Under the 16d minimum guard the usable instant is M/31 - the promise day itself - leaving a 1-day INTRADAY leak window (a decision during M/31 trading hours can precede the posting later that day). 30-day months: promise M/30 = bound, 16d guard closes it. February: bound M/30 lands 1-2 days AFTER the promise (wrong-side conservative, safe but late). (b) 'b' files, month M (settlements M/16..M/last): page promises 'about the 15th of the next month'. 31-day months: bound M/31+15 = M+1/15, 16d guard usable M+1/16 - closed. 30-day months (4 of 12): bound M/30+15 = M+1/14 - 1 day BEFORE the promised 15th; 16d-guard usable instant M+1/15 = promise day = same 1-day intraday leak window. (c) Independently, 'We cannot guarantee that the data will be posted by a particular date' makes ANY fixed bound formally optimistic in the late direction; late posting is a conservatism cost only (a decision may forgo a usable file), NOT a leak - the leak direction opens only where bound+guard < promise, which is exactly the two month-length classes above. Net: the 16-day MINIMUM guard carries a same-day leak window for ~11 of 24 half-month files per year (46%: 'a' files of 31-day months + 'b' files of 30-day months); the 17-day guard closes every class, and 18d covers holiday-drift clusters. This does NOT overturn the lane posture (control-only, conservative, RETROSPECTIVE_ONLY historical use already frozen) - it HARDENS it: the 17-18d guard must be BINDING in any successor S4 PIT audit, not advisory.
